findings.summary: NACA now sets the pooled median. OCR remains 85.5% of its call; shared admission leaves no vLLM request queue, but each GPU averages only about three running requests.
observations: This profile uses the completed available_gpu_8 configuration: four L4 GPUs, server concurrency eight, global admission eight per GPU, four per worker/GPU, four n-gram proposals, compiled BF16 embeddings and the unchanged frozen references.

One warm-up, three ordinary calls and a separate complete instrumented call passed. Diagnostic median is 2.987 s: OCR 2.550 s and embedding 0.297 s. Mean stage shares are 85.5% OCR and 9.9% embedding. These calls are separate from evaluator samples.

Within OCR windows, 100-ms scheduler samples show mean running requests of 2.95, 3.43, 3.07 and 3.12 on GPUs 0–3. Each reaches eight briefly; maximum waiting is zero. No preemptions occur, and peak KV-cache occupancy is below 0.64%. Startup and request draining also contribute to low occupancy; these counts alone do not prove host starvation.

Generated-token totals vary by routing: [702,1187,910,1029], [920,803,1112,993] and [801,1360,759,908]. Every call processes 71 regions. The admission limits are respected and every completed PDF leaves zero pending or active leases.

N-gram acceptance is only 2.01–2.89% across GPUs, yielding 1.08–1.12 tokens per verification step. Verification steps plus accepted proposals plus the initial token per region exactly account for all raw generated tokens in the ordinary calls.

OCR-window GPU busy averages 68.9%, 83.3%, 68.3%, 84.0%, with only seven one-second samples per GPU. Mean power is about 64–67 W at the fixed 72 W limit. The short sampling windows do not establish peak compute or bandwidth saturation.
All four bounded traces contain kernels; the complete instrumented OCR, chunks and embeddings match the frozen requirements. Scheduler and raw-token accounting are saved in scheduler-accounting.json.

Persistent matmul accounts for 68–70% of recorded kernel duration in the bounded capture, including vision prefill. The decoder-only share is not isolated. A separate synthetic BF16 matrix screen passed 140 bitwise cases and motivates smaller decoder tiles; raw samples are in decoder-matmul-screen.json.
findings.next_step: Four admission slots regressed and twelve was within prior repeat variation, so retain eight. Test smaller BF16 decoder matrix tiles against a fresh default-tile control, preserving batch invariance and all frozen evaluator checks.
findings.optimization: Eight is the fresh control. Four permits fewer active requests and may improve late assignment; twelve can queue work behind the eight-request server. Neither improvement is assumed from occupancy alone.
